enquiry: Our NIR moisture model was built for wheat flour. We now also mill rye and oat flour, and our instrument supplier says the same model will work because water absorbs the same way in every flour. We would like to start using it on the new flours next week.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with moisture measurement on rye and oat flour, and what decision should the real-time moisture value drive?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies whether the need is routine control, quality release or documentation, which sets how much validation is needed before use.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision unknown; treat the model as provisional for screening only until the decision is defined.

clarification_questions.question: What moisture level and range do you expect in rye flour and oat flour, and how does it compare with wheat flour?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the wheat model's calibration range covers the new flours at all.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Moisture level unknown; lab screening establishes whether the wheat calibration range covers rye and oat flour.

clarification_questions.question: How are the rye and oat flours presented to the NIR instrument (dry powder, sieved, tempered), and do they differ in colour, bran content or particle size from wheat flour?
clarification_questions.why: Physical differences in particle size and scattering change the NIR signal independently of moisture.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Physical properties unknown; assume they differ from wheat until lab screening shows otherwise.

clarification_questions.question: Are the rye and oat flours processed under different conditions (temperature, milling method, storage) than wheat flour?
clarification_questions.why: Process differences can change the sample matrix and the relation between spectrum and moisture.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Conditions unknown; the wheat model is assumed not transferable until checked.

clarification_questions.question: Where and how is the NIR measurement made (at-line, inline, fibre probe, distance to the analyzer)?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the measurement geometry and whether the same instrument setup is used for the new flours.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Setup unknown; assume the same instrument and geometry as for wheat flour.

clarification_questions.question: Which reference laboratory method is used for moisture, and what is its accuracy on each flour type?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference method for rye and oat flour, the model cannot be checked on the new products.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; no validation is possible until a reference method is agreed.

clarification_questions.question: Do you have reference-analysed rye and oat flour samples covering the moisture range, and can they be measured in the same run?
clarification_questions.why: Independent samples are needed to test whether the wheat model predicts rye and oat flour correctly.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Samples unavailable; screening cannot start and the model stays unvalidated for these flours.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy and response time are required for moisture on rye and oat flour, and what is the acceptance criterion?
clarification_questions.why: Sets whether the wheat model can be accepted as is, or needs recalibration or a new model.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Accuracy requirement unknown; no acceptance criterion can be set yet.

clarification_questions.question: What is the current performance of the wheat model, and is the next week start a fixed deadline or a preference?
clarification_questions.why: Shows the baseline to compare against and whether a short validation is feasible before use.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Baseline and deadline unknown; plan a lab check before any production use.

not_supported: S02 p.12 shows a NIR-LED moisture sensor, a wood-surface drying demo, and SNV-corrected spectra of starch, flour and sugar. It does not show moisture measurement in powders with diffuse reflection, so 'supports NIR diffuse reflection for moisture in powders' goes beyond the page. Fix: Say the page shows a NIR-LED moisture sensor with trans-flex or diffuse reflection options, a wood-surface demo, and flour spectra, but no powder moisture result.

not_supported: The Raman 'full range' classification relies on S02 p.6, which gives only fiber transmission ranges. DOCX §5 says Raman range is set by the laser excitation and shift, which is not stated on the cited pages, so the Raman coverage judgement is not supported. Fix: Limit the Raman fiber check to the stated 785 nm excitation and the actual Raman shift window, or cite the page that defines the Raman spectral window.

not_supported: The cited DOCX §5 page does not mention a wheat calibration or flour at all. It only says NIR calibration is matrix-specific, so the wheat-specific premise is not on the cited page. Fix: Cite the source that documents the wheat calibration, or rephrase as a general matrix-specific calibration risk for rye and oat flour.
